effect: A war's cost in public opinion now depends on the country's role, and being attacked brings a rally. Every participant paid the same 7 approval and 5 stability per war, plus exhaustion, with no rally for the attacked. Now the aggressor pays in full and every other fighting member 70%; exhaustion is unchanged, so long, costly wars still wear governments down. Countries in a support role are not counted as at war, as before. The country directly attacked in a war that began during play also gets a rally of up to 6 approval and 3 stability, halving every 90 days, taken from its strongest such war; AI allies who join it do not. Real rallies are short and sizeable, and scale with being attacked (from memory). The weights and the rally are tuning choices. Wars already under way at the start, which record days of war before day 0 in a field kept through save and reload, get no rally. A player who joins on the attacked side, or takes over from the attacked country, becomes that war's principal and so gets the rally too. Expected effect: attackers pay more than defenders, and a government invaded out of the blue gains support for some months. Day 0 unchanged: the approval anchor is measured with the same terms. No new state. (Minified names in this text are those of build 26403824; the patch's find text has the current ones.)
